covered_by.title: Arxiv/1609.08688: fix five misformalisations in sIncreasingrTuples
covered_by.note: The PR makes IsComparableSet₂ universally quantified over distinct pairs, restates maximalLength_le_isBigO with an explicit c > 0 and eventual bound, moves the lex tag onto the coordinate pairs in tripleProduct/sequenceProduct (codomain Fin 3 → α ×ₗ α), and changes maximalLength_pow to ∃ᶠ, adding a separate eventual version at a lower exponent. This is exactly the set of five defects we flagged, with the fixes we suggested (the PR credits our review).

covered_by.title: SpectralSets: require positive measure in spectralPair
covered_by.note: Adds `(interior (A : Set (Fin n → ℝ))).Nonempty →` to the shared helper `spectralProductImpliesRightSpectral` (exactly our suggested fix) and additionally requires positive measure in `spectralPair` elsewhere. All five of our findings stem from the degenerate-left-factor defect in this helper, so the PR covers them all.

covered_by.title: Likely misformalization in `Arxiv/2209.04540/SpectralSetsAndWeakTiling.lean`
covered_by.note: Reports that Mathlib's `ConvexBody` admits singletons and null sets are vacuously spectral, so with A = {0} the helper asserts every bounded measurable B is spectral; suggests requiring nonempty interior or positive volume of A. Identical underlying defect and fix to ours; the issue names only the `of_convexBody` and `three_dimensional` statements explicitly, but the defect is in the shared helper so all five findings are the same problem.

covered_by.title: fix(Books/Equidistribution): ask the transcendental equidistribution question rather than assert it
covered_by.note: The PR targets the same declaration and the same defect: the universal claim over all transcendental x is false and unsupported by the cited almost-everywhere result. Its repair turns the assertion into an `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ x, Transcendental ℚ x → ...` question rather than restating the a.e. theorem as we suggest, but the underlying problem it fixes is exactly ours.

covered_by.title: Books/Equidistribution: `isEquidistributedModuloOne_transcendental_three_halves_pow` is false as written — the cited source says "almost all", not "every transcendental"
covered_by.note: Reports that the declaration is false as written because the source says 'almost all', not 'every transcendental', and gives an explicit Cantor-set counterexample (density ≥ 1/8 in [0,1/10]); our finding is the same defect with a Flatto–Lagarias–Pollington counterexample instead.

covered_by.title: fix(ErdosProblems/1095): log g(k) ≍ k / log k is a Θ statement
covered_by.note: Replaces `~[atTop]` with `=Θ[atTop]` in erdos_1095.variants.log_equivalent, exactly the change our finding asks for (the source's ≍ is a Θ statement, not asymptotic equivalence). Cites the fc-review audit.

covered_by.title: fix(ErdosProblems/1167): add the target condition κ_α > r
covered_by.note: Adds the hypothesis r < κ α (2 < κ α in the r = 2 variant) to erdos_1167, binary_colors and r_eq_two, with the same (2, ℵ₁) counterexample we gave; this is exactly the omitted target restriction in all three of our findings.

covered_by.title: Tracking: possible misformalizations found in statement audits
covered_by.note: Multi-file tracking issue, but its entry 'Erdős 1167 — omitted κ α > r condition' names precisely the missing restriction behind all three of our findings on this file (fixed by PR 5492).

covered_by.title: Erdős 295: fix off-by-one in the definition of k(N)
covered_by.note: Changes exists_k from Fin k.succ to Fin k so Nat.find gives the actual number of unit fractions (k 1 = 1, k 2 = 3); this is exactly our off-by-one finding and even credits the same source of the report.

covered_by.title: fix: preserve repeated terms in Erdős 348
covered_by.note: Replaces `IsAddComplete (Set.range (Function.updateFinset a s 0))` by `IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (Function.updateFinset a s 0)` in both clauses so repeated terms are preserved — exactly our suggested fix for the multiplicity-losing defect.

covered_by.title: Erdős 348 loses repeated terms in its completeness checks
covered_by.note: Reports that `Set.range` discards repeated values so the completeness checks lose multiplicities, and proposes `IsAddCompleteNatSeq'` in both clauses; the same defect and fix as our finding.

covered_by.title: fix(ErdosProblems/386): let k vary with n
covered_by.note: Moves `∃ k ≥ 2` inside `∃ᶠ n in atTop` in erdos_386 so k may vary with n, which is precisely the quantifier-order defect our finding describes. Cites the fc-review audit.

covered_by.title: fix(ErdosProblems/516): strictly increasing exponents in the Kövari variant
covered_by.note: Adds `(hmono : StrictMono n)` to `limsup_ratio_eq_one` with a docstring explaining that repeated exponents allow cancellation to f = 0; the same counterexample family and the fix we suggested.

covered_by.title: fix(ErdosProblems/697): correct thresholds and zero case
covered_by.note: Adds `hm : 0 < m` to `variants.delta_lt` and swaps the threshold inequalities in `parts.i` (now `α < 1/log 2`) and `parts.ii` (now `1/log 2 < α`), exactly the three corrections our findings ask for.

covered_by.title: Tracking: possible misformalizations found in statement audits
covered_by.note: Tracking issue whose entry 'Erdős 697 — reversed thresholds and the m = 0 case' names both defects we found: the reversed thresholds in parts.i/parts.ii and the m = 0 case of variants.delta_lt. Only a one-line triage lead, but it covers all our findings on this file.

covered_by.title: fix(ErdosProblems/726): take the remainder in ℕ before casting
covered_by.note: Changes the filter to `((n % p : ℕ) : ℝ)` so the remainder is taken in ℕ before casting, fixing the real-field-remainder-is-zero defect our finding reports; includes the same Lean counterexample. Cites the fc-review audit.

covered_by.title: fix: lower density in Erdős 851
covered_by.note: Replaces the conclusion ∃ r d, HasDensity d ∧ 1 - ε ≤ d by ∃ r, 1 - ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity, exactly our suggested fix for the spurious density-existence requirement.

covered_by.title: Erdős 851: "the density ... is at least"
covered_by.note: Reports that 'the density ... is at least 1 - ε' should be read as a lower-density bound rather than existence of a natural density; same defect as our finding, fixed by PR 5364.

covered_by.title: Erdős 897: fix growth hypothesis, log-growth conclusion and additive …
covered_by.note: The PR replaces the joint (p, k) product-filter limsup in all four statements with a limsup over prime powers q → ∞ (LimsupPrimePowEqTop, essentially our suggested formula), changes log_growth's conclusion from ≤ to =, and replaces the k-unrestricted `f (p^k) = f p` disjunct with IsStronglyAdditive (k ≥ 1) or IsCompletelyAdditive. Those are exactly our five findings (the PR credits our review).

covered_by.title: fix(Erdos/939): state the second question as finiteness; r ≥ 6 infinitude
covered_by.note: Replaces `variants.infinite : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939Sums r).Infinite` with `variants.finite : answer(False) ↔ ∀ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939Sums r).Finite`, the source's finiteness question, and records the r ≥ 6 construction separately as `infinite_of_six_le`; this is our suggested fix (and the PR body cites our review).

covered_by.title: Green 21: positive arity in the Fox–Kleitman modular question
covered_by.note: Adds 0 < k to the quantifier prefix of fox_kleitman_modular, citing the k = 0, p = 2 empty-tuple refutation; this is our finding and suggested fix (the PR also tweaks the RadoCondition docstring and a page range, which are incidental).

covered_by.title: fix(GreensOpenProblems/32): dirichlet_regime needs ⌊ω p⌋₊ > 100
covered_by.note: Merged after our commit; changes the dirichlet_regime hypothesis from `100 < ω p` to `101 ≤ ω p`, with the same rounding counterexample (100 < ω p < 101 gives ⌊ω p⌋₊ = 100 and a required gap of p − 1) that our finding gives, and the fix we suggested.

covered_by.title: fix(Mathoverflow/31809): ask for a pretriangulated category that is not triangulated
covered_by.note: Negates the right-hand side of `mathoverflow_31809` so `answer(True)` means a pretriangulated non-triangulated category exists, which is exactly our finding and suggested fix (the PR cites our review).

covered_by.title: fix(OEIS/100475): ask the existential question for positive starts
covered_by.note: Rewrites conjecture as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ x, 0 < x ∧ x ≠ 1 ∧ IsUltimatelyPeriodic (aStartAt x)`, addressing both of our findings on this declaration: the answer slot scoped under the binder x, and the admission of the artificial x = 0 fixed point (recorded separately as conjecture_with_zero).

covered_by.title: fix(OEIS/167918): ask whether the ratio is bounded, state existence
covered_by.note: Restates conjecture2 as answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C, ∀ n > 0, S (a n) / S n ≤ C, matching our suggested fix (it also drops the existence hypothesis and adds a separate conjecture_infinite, which go beyond our finding).

covered_by.title: Likely misformalization in `Wikipedia/BatemanHornConjecture.lean`
covered_by.note: Reports that `BatemanHornConstant` uses Mathlib's unconditional `∏'`, which is not `Multipliable` for the conditionally convergent Euler product and so evaluates to the junk value 1 (constant 1/2 for X²+1), and backs it with a cheap Lean disproof of `bateman_horn_conjecture`. Same declaration, same defect and the same suggested fix (ordered/cutoff product).

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/Bloch): a schlicht disk is the image of an open subdomain
covered_by.note: Requires `IsOpen S` and `f '' S = ball x B` in blochRadius, blochConstant and univalentBlochConstant, closing the arbitrary-subset gap that made blochConstant equal landauConstant. Our three findings on the bound/exact-value theorems are consequences of the definitional defect and their suggested fix is to correct blochConstant, so this PR covers all five.

covered_by.title: Likely misformalization in `Wikipedia/Bloch.lean`
covered_by.note: Reports (via a cheap disproof of blochConstant_exact_value) that S being an arbitrary subset makes InjOn vacuous and collapses the Bloch constant onto the Landau constant in blochRadius, blochConstant and univalentBlochConstant, suggesting open (connected) S. This is the same underlying defect behind all five of our findings.

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/Falconer): falconer_conjecture is false at d = 1
covered_by.note: Adds (h2d : 2 ≤ d) to falconer_conjecture and documents a base-7 Cantor-set counterexample at d = 1 (ours used base 6); same missing dimension restriction as our finding.

covered_by.title: Wikipedia/HardyLittlewood: `first_hardy_littlewood_conjecture` states `=O` where the source states `∼`, and does not require the offsets distinct
covered_by.note: Reports the same two independent defects: FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor states =O[atTop] where the source states ∼ (making the constant irrelevant and the surviving bound a classical sieve theorem), and first_hardy_littlewood_conjecture does not require distinct offsets, with the same ![0, 1, 1] example (divergent Euler product, tprod junk value, wrong log exponent for the twin-prime count).

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/Kakeya): require positive dimension in kakeya_finite
covered_by.note: Adds `(hn : 0 < n)` to `kakeya_finite` because the empty set is a Kakeya set in dimension 0 and the bound reads 1 ≤ 0; identical to our finding and fix (the PR cites our audit page).

covered_by.title: Kaplansky: use ordinary torsion-freeness, not IsMulTorsionFree
covered_by.note: Draft PR replacing `IsMulTorsionFree` (unique roots) with a reintroduced `Monoid.IsTorsionFree` (no nontrivial finite-order elements) in the shared variable and in `promislow_group_is_torsionfree`, `counter_unit_conjecture` and `counter_unit_conjecture_weak`, noting the Promislow counterexample `(a²b)² = b²`. This is exactly our defect on all five declarations (the PR cites our review).

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/ModularityConjecture): use period 1 in the q-expansion
covered_by.note: Changes modularFormAn to (qExpansion 1 f).coeff n because the first argument of qExpansion is the period, not the level, with the same a₁ = 0 for N > 1 / zero space at N = 1 argument; exactly our finding and suggested fix.

covered_by.title: fix(MovingSofa): apply translation before rotation
covered_by.note: Draft PR (refs issue 5270) that reverses the composition in rotateTranslate to `(vaddConst p).trans rotation` so that rotateTranslate α p q = R_α (q + p), and adds an rfl regression theorem; this is the fix our finding proposes. It is marked draft pending confirmation of the intended convention, whereas our finding shows via the Gerver path constants that the current order yields an empty gerversSofa, so the reversal is the correct choice.

covered_by.title: MovingSofa: rotateTranslate implements the opposite composition order from its documented convention
covered_by.note: Reports that rotateTranslate acts as q ↦ R_α q + p rather than the documented R_α (q + p) because AffineIsometryEquiv.trans applies its left argument first, and derives x_R(t) = R_t p_G(t) for the file's path, i.e. the current order does not produce Romik's hallway family; suggests reversing the composition or supplying R_α p. Same defect and same fix as our finding.

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/RudinsConjecture): state uniqueness at N = GP_k + 1 ≥ 8
covered_by.note: Replaces `6 ≤ N` with `8 ≤ N` plus `∃ k : ℤ, N = k(3k-1)/2 + 1` (generalized pentagonal + 1), restricting uniqueness to the lengths the super-strong conjecture covers, with the N = 6 counterexample 120n + 49; this is our finding and suggested fix.

covered_by.title: Wikipedia/UnionClosed: `cardinality_even_of_union_closed_tight` assumes every element hits half the family, which is stronger than "tight" (and forces `n` finite)
covered_by.note: Reports that UCC_tight's `∀ i, #{x ∈ A | i ∈ x} = #A/2` is stronger than tightness (max over i equals #A/2), with an enumeration showing the gap; this is exactly our finding. It additionally notes the hypothesis forces n finite and a shadowed binder, which go beyond what we flagged.

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/WallSunSun): the Lucas parameters must not vary with p
covered_by.note: Identifies the same defect (Lucas parameters existentially chosen per prime make the set trivially infinite), proves the original statement and reclassifies it as solved, and adds a new open declaration fixing (a, b) before p. Our finding cautions that merely fixing arbitrary (a, b) still admits degenerate choices such as a = 0, so the replacement may need further work, but the defect addressed is the one we found.

covered_by.title: Wikipedia/WallSunSun: infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq is elementary because its Lucas parameters vary with p
covered_by.note: Reports that infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq is elementary because a, b vary with p, giving the same a = p² (or 2p²) construction and a Lean proof; same defect as our finding, addressed by PR 5550.
